breakingChanges: Key segments are now validated for every application. A setting code, the `settingCode` and `code` of master data, and the `userId` and `groupId` of group and user settings must be non-empty and must not contain `#` or `@`, and a setting code must not be `MASTER_SETTING`. Otherwise every create, upsert and bulk request, `getSetting` (`GET /api/master-setting/:code`) and `MasterDataService.list` (`GET /api/master-data`) return 400. Updates and deletes by key (`PATCH`/`DELETE /api/master-setting/:pk/:sk`, `PUT`/`DELETE /api/master-data/:pk/:sk`) also reject a sort key that contains `@`. Rows already stored with `@` in their key are therefore no longer reachable through the API and must be re-created under a valid key

Setting rows and data rows are now changed only through their own routes. `PUT`/`DELETE /api/master-data/:pk/:sk` (`MasterDataService.update`/`delete`) reject a `MASTER_SETTING#...` key, and `PATCH`/`DELETE /api/master-setting/:pk/:sk` (`MasterSettingService.updateSetting`/`deleteSetting`) reject a key that is not `MASTER_SETTING#` followed by a code. Group and user keys such as `MASTER_SETTING#USER#u1#S1` are still accepted

Master copy is restricted to system administrators. With `controllerAuth` set, `POST /api/master-setting/copy` requires the `system_admin` role from the `custom:roles` claim; roles in `controllerAuth.write` and group-derived roles do not allow it. With an access resolver registered, `MasterSettingService.copy` also requires a write grant whose `systemId` and `settingCode` are both `*`

`POST /api/master-bulk` now upserts the settings first and the data rows after, instead of both at once, so data rows can use a setting created in the same request. The keys of every item are validated before the first write, but the request is not atomic across settings and data: with an access resolver registered, the access checks of the data items run after the settings are written, so a forbidden data item fails the request and leaves the settings written

`GET /api/tasks/sfn-task-parent` now resolves the tenant like the rest of the framework: the `custom:tenant` claim wins over the `x-tenant-code` header. It used to read a `custom:tenant_code` claim that nobody sets, so it always took the tenant from the header
features: Add the opt-in `controllerAuth` module option, which guards the built-in master routes. Reads need a role in `read` (default: any logged-in user), writes need a role in `write` (default: `system_admin`), and the requested tenant must be the caller's tenant unless the request only reads the common tenant or the caller has a cross-tenant role. Without it the routes stay unguarded and the module logs a startup warning

Scope master data per system. A master setting can carry a `systemId` (stored in lower case; `shared` is reserved for data every system receives), and its data rows inherit it. Register one class with `@MasterAccessResolver()` to grant read and write per system and per setting. The services then check the grants in every method, and the list endpoints filter in the SQL query, so pagination and totals stay correct

Add `GET /api/master-access`, which tells a UI whether access control is enabled and returns the caller's grants, and `MasterSettingService.assignSystem`, which tags existing untagged rows of a setting code with a `systemId`
Add `includeCommon` to the master setting and master data list searches. It adds the common tenant's rows whose code the caller's tenant does not have

Add the `commonTenantCode` module option (the tenant that holds common master data, default `common`) and the `enableCopyTask` module option (registers the master copy handler, default: the value of `enableController`)
Add a nullable `system_id` column to the RDS master table of the project template, written by the template's RDS handler, and return `systemId` at the top level of API responses
Add the `databaseProvider` module option (`postgresql` or `mysql`). By default it is detected from the Prisma client
bugFixes: Master copy now reads data from the source setting's tenant. It used to read from a hard-coded `meltec` tenant

Master copy now copies sequences. Both keys used to be built from the target tenant, so nothing was ever copied. A target sequence behind the source jumps to the source's value; the write is conditional, so a target that issued numbers in the meantime is never moved back

Name, code and keyword searches failed on MySQL, the default database of `mbc new`, because they always sent the PostgreSQL-only `mode: 'insensitive'`. The setting description search used a JSON path that fit neither database; it now uses `['description']` on PostgreSQL and `'$.description'` on MySQL
A setting update that omits `settingValue` no longer clears the setting's attributes, one that omits `name` keeps the name, and a master data update that omits `seq` keeps it

features: Add the protected `CommandService.getCommandAdmissionConditions` hook for atomic command admission. A `CommandService` subclass can return DynamoDB `ConditionCheck` entries, which are committed with the initial command write in a single `TransactWriteItems` request. A command is then accepted only if, for example, a maintenance gate is still open at the generation the request observed, which closes the race between a preflight gate check and a gate that closes in the meantime. The default returns no checks and keeps the plain `PutItem` path, so existing apps behave as before

Add `CommandAdmissionRejectedException` (HTTP 409) for a failed admission check and `CommandAdmissionContentionException` (HTTP 503) for a transaction cancelled by `TransactionConflict`. A version conflict on the command write is still reported as `ConditionalCheckFailedException` (409), and any other cancellation is rethrown as the original `TransactionCanceledException` (500). Core does not retry
The infrastructure template now grants `dynamodb:ConditionCheckItem` on the stack-prefixed DynamoDB tables, which the admission transaction needs on witness tables

breakingChanges: Require Node.js 22 or later (`engines.node` is now `>=22`). Node.js 18 and 20 are end of life and will not receive the fix for CVE-2026-111497 (Node2Shell), a remote code execution vulnerability in the Brotli decoder bundled with Node.js. The fix ships in Node.js 22.23.4, 24.22.1 and 26.12.1. `@mbc-cqrs-serverless/core` also now depends on nodemailer 10, which itself requires Node.js 20 or later. CI tests Node.js 22 and 24

nodemailer 10 ships its own type definitions, and its default export is no longer a namespace. Code that uses `nodemailer.SendMailOptions`, `nodemailer.Transporter` or `nodemailer.SentMessageInfo` must import these types by name from `nodemailer` instead, and `@types/nodemailer` should be removed. Apps that only use `EmailService` need no code changes

New projects use Node.js 22. The Lambda function and layer use `NODEJS_22_X`, the Docker image is based on `node:22-bookworm-slim` and installs `openssl` (Prisma's query engine needs libssl, which bookworm-slim does not ship), the `infra-local` images use `node:22-alpine`, and `serverless.yml` uses `nodejs22.x` with serverless-offline `^13.9.0`. The CDK pipeline pins Node.js 22 for its CodeBuild projects, and `@types/node` moves to 22
security: Clear high and critical advisories in production dependencies: proxy-addr 2.0.8, body-parser 1.20.9 / 2.4.0, multer 2.5.0, nodemailer 10.3.1, @modelcontextprotocol/sdk 1.32.2, zod 4.6.7

The CLI project template's dependency overrides now also pin proxy-addr 2.0.8, body-parser 1.20.9 / 2.4.0 and multer 2.5.0, so newly scaffolded projects no longer ship these advisories. The `qs` override, in the framework and the template, moves to `^6.16.1`, the minimum that the patched body-parser and express 5 require

breakingChanges: Replace LocalStack with Floci (`floci/floci:1.6.0`) as the local S3 emulator in the scaffolded local development stack. LocalStack Community Edition reached end of life in March 2026. Floci serves S3 on the same port (`4566`) with path-style addressing, so application code and `.env` values do not change, and deployed environments are not affected
features: `DirectoryService` methods now take `ICommandOptions` instead of an options type that only allowed `invokeContext`, so callers can pass `source` and `requestId` through to the command for tracing. Backward compatible: `invokeContext` is still the only required field
bugFixes: Fix `mbc new` failing at dependency installation with `EOVERRIDE: Override for js-yaml@^4.1.0 conflicts with direct dependency` (broken since v1.3.5). The template's `js-yaml` override now references the direct dependency, which moves to `^4.3.2` and also clears a high-severity `js-yaml` advisory

Fix `npm run migrate` in newly scaffolded projects. Prisma does not expand the `:-` default syntax used for `LOCAL_RDS_PORT` in `DATABASE_URL` (`P1013`), and `prisma/ddb.ts` did not expand the endpoint variables at all (`Invalid URL`). Existing projects can apply the same fix: reference `LOCAL_RDS_PORT` without a `:-` default in `DATABASE_URL`, and load `.env` in `prisma/ddb.ts` with `expand(dotenv.config())` from `dotenv-expand`

Ship the Claude Code skills in the published npm package. They were missing from the package, so `mbc install-skills` and the manual `cp -r node_modules/@mbc-cqrs-serverless/mcp-server/skills/*` step could not find them
